data.reasoning: The package is a standard Go application build with pinned sources (tagged GitHub release) and verified checksums (SHA256/MD5). The PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments and standard build/package functions with no executable code in global scope, no suspicious network requests, no obfuscation, and no execution of fetched content. The .SRCINFO and .gitignore are benign metadata/config files. The 'inconclusive' verdict from the first report was caused by a transient LLM API error (HTTP 400) when processing .SRCINFO, not by any security concern. The second report successfully analyzed all files and correctly found no issues.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is purely a tool failure artifact. The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit .SRCINFO, causing it to mark that file as inconclusive and the overall result as inconclusive. The deepseek model successfully processed all three files without error. There is no substantive disagreement about security findings—both models that successfully analyzed the PKGBUILD found it safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to process .SRCINFO due to LLM API error (HTTP 400), resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from security-related inconclusive findings in the final verdict calculation. A transient infrastructure error should not override successful analysis of the same files by other models.

When aggregating multi-model results, implement fallback logic: if one model fails on a file due to a tool error but another model successfully analyzes that same file, the successful analysis should be used rather than marking the overall result as inconclusive.
The audit tool should track and report tool errors separately from security findings to prevent infrastructure issues from being misinterpreted as security concerns.
